extracted.intended_audience: F99/K00 fellowship reviewers, mentors, and grant program officers
extracted.subtask_description: A predoctoral-to-postdoctoral (F99/K00) fellowship application describing training goals, planned activities, specific aims, and research strategy to study how living environments and ICT influence social isolation and cognitive decline in older adults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Goal 1: Increase knowledge in prevention, intervention and policy pertaining cognitive decline in normal aging and the development of ADRD
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Goal 1: Increase knowledge in prevention, intervention and policy pertain cognitive decline in normal aging and the development of ADRD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities listed: Course PM-605 Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (Spring); conduct a systematic literature review on mechanisms linking social isolation and cognitive decline; Course GERO-566 Cognitive Decline: Alzheimer's Disease and Dementia (Spring); attend training sessions provided by USC ADRC Research and Education Core (REC); clinical internship with neurologists at memory clinics; join monthly OADC investigator meetings (online in F99, in-person in K00). Mentorship: Dr. Ringman (USC) for F99 clinical internship and Dr. Kaye (OHSU) for K00. Dr. Dodge and Dr. Silbert provide directed reading and liaison to OADC resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a systematic review and develop a literature database
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a database of literature and conduct a systematic review of literature on the underlying mechanisms of the association between social isolation and cognitive decline. Applicant will lead the writing of the systematic review manuscript as first-author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit expectation to produce a first-author systematic review manuscript; course enrollment (PM-605) supports this activity. This is positioned as foundational to discover mechanisms (social behavioral and biological) to be followed up in empirical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical internships and clinical exposure to memory care services
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete clinical internships in memory care clinics mentored by neurologists to gain understanding of current screening, treatment, and health services for older adults at risk of ADRD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors named (Dr. John Ringman at USC ADRC for F99; Dr. Jeffrey Kaye at OHSU ADC for K00). Participation in clinical internships and investigator meetings to observe screening/treatment workflows and health services context relevant to intervention design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Goal 2: Gain methodological skills for investigating mechanisms (longitudinal and neuroimaging methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gain methodological skills for investigating the underlying mechanism of how social isolation influences cognitive health in diverse environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific methods & training: analyzing longitudinal data with Structural Equation Modeling and Multilevel Modeling; conduct dissertation research using five waves of NHATS to prepare for causal inference analysis; take PM-560 Statistical Programming with R to improve efficiency and collaboration; familiarize with neuroimaging outcomes in F99 via collaborator datasets; receive training in volumetric and functional MRI; interpret neuroimaging results with Dr. Silbert; attend OADC imaging core weekly lab meetings and AAIC Neuroimaging pre-conference workshop; collaborate with neuroimaging experts and use I-CONECT data for hands-on experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Goal 3: Explore technology-based interventions and digital biomarkers
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore future directions for harnessing technology to promote a positive aging experience, including using mobile health, virtual reality, and wearable/digital biomarkers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities: participate in IMTOP and CSMP research projects; contribute to developing health behavior-change-theory guided mHealth interventions; receive training on assessing user engagement and intervention effectiveness; observe virtual reality intervention sessions; learn about digital biomarker collection and analysis through CART and I-CONECT (e.g., ambient sensors for walking speed, electronic pillboxes). Aim to design wearable device-based intervention studies and incorporate high-frequency digital biomarker data into ADRD research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Goal 4: Design, evaluate, and implement community-based interventions (mixed-methods & implementation science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to design, evaluate, and implement community-based interventions using mixed-methods and implementation science approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations and activities: observe I-CONECT fieldwork and conduct conversational intervention sessions; work with community-based organizations with Dr. Chi; use mixed-methods (training taken with Dr. Palinkas) to solicit older adults' and stakeholders' perspectives; formulate purposeful sampling plans and design interview guides; receive direct qualitative data analysis training (biweekly meetings in F99, monthly in K00); consult on intervention implementation and implementation science considerations to improve intervention effectiveness; participate in Clinical Trial and Methods PIA, IMPACT-AD course, Study Designs for Intervention Research in Real-World Settings (UCSF), and NINDS-sponsored Clinical Trial Methodology Course (R25NS088248).

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned allocation of effort and timeline (percent effort expectations)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the proposed F99 and K00 phases, 75% of effort will be dedicated to research activities with specified percentages for teaching, coursework, grant writing, and conferences varying by year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 example allocations: F99-Year1: Research 75%, Teaching 5%, Coursework 10%, Grant writing 5%, Conferences 5%. K00-Year1 and subsequent years show Research 75%, Teaching 0–5%, Coursework 0–5%, Grant writing 15–20% (notably 20% in K00-Year3 for K99/R00 development), Conferences 5%. Use these allocations to demonstrate protected research time and progression toward grantsmanship milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional development and grantmanship activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in professional development to prepare for faculty applications and independent funding, including manuscript preparation, grant writing courses, and proposal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific actions: prepare and submit manuscripts to high-impact peer-reviewed journals; attend 'Design Studio' and Advanced Grant Writing Course at OHSU; participate in peer-support writing groups; complete Responsible Conduct of Research seminars; allocate time to develop a K99/R00 application (target year 3 of K00) and submit to pilot funding (R21/mini R01) to collect preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aim 1 (dissertation): Examine living environment, ICT use, social isolation, and cognitive health using longitudinal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1: Dissertation project will examine the effect of physical and social environments of living on social isolation and cognitive health, and investigate effects of ICT use within living environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach: use five waves of NHATS longitudinal data; investigate moderation by ICT use for medical, social, and instrumental purposes within living contexts. Aim is to generate longitudinal evidence on environmental impacts on social isolation and cognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aim 2 (postdoctoral): Build knowledge on mechanisms and develop a technology-facilitated behavioral intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 2: Postdoctoral research will build knowledge on behavioral and contextual pathways explaining the association between social isolation and cognitive decline and develop a technology-facilitated behavioral health intervention using community participatory co-design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach: use I-CONECT trial data (digital biomarkers, neuroimaging) and CART initiative data; recruit I-CONECT participants to co-design intervention via mixed-methods; produce a protocol for a technology-facilitated behavioral intervention to reduce social isolation and prevent cognitive decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct definitions and measurement considerations (social isolation, physical & social environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and measurement guidance: Social isolation is 'the absence of contact with others, lack of relationships and social integration.' Living environment includes physical (objective neighborhood aspects like access to amenities, green spaces, aesthetics) and social (social participation and perceived integration) dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalization guidance: measure physical environment via community and in-home disorder, outdoor spaces & public buildings, common areas; measure social environment via perceived neighborhood cohesion, sense of belongingness, trust, social participation. The proposal emphasizes longitudinal measurement rather than cross-sectional and links measurement choices to hypothesized mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses to be tested (H1–H9) regarding environment, social isolation, ICT, and cognitive health
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of nine explicit hypotheses: H1–H9 describe predicted longitudinal relationships among physical environment, social environment, social isolation, ICT use (social/instrumental/medical), and cognitive health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses listed verbatim in the proposal: H1: Negative physical characteristics (community/home disorder) associated with increase in social isolation longitudinally. H2: Positive social environment factors associated with less social isolation longitudinally. H3: Social environment buffers the influence of physical environment on social isolation over time. H4: Disadvantaged physical environments predict deterioration in cognitive health over time. H5: Positive social environment has a direct longitudinal effect on cognitive health. H6: Social isolation partially mediates the association between physical/social environments and cognitive health over time. H7: ICT use for social purposes alleviate social isolation over time. H8: ICT use for non-social purposes is not related to social isolation longitudinally. H9: ICT use buffers the longitudinal association between physical/social environments and social isolation. These hypotheses define the evaluation targets for the empirical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICT mechanisms and differential effects of ICT use
rubrics_metrics.description: ICT may alleviate social isolation through four mechanisms and may have differential effects depending on purpose and duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the systematic review cited: ICT alleviates elderly social isolation by (1) connecting to the outside world, (2) gaining social support, (3) engaging in activities of interest, and (4) boosting self-confidence. Note: existing evidence suggests ICT interventions' effects may not last beyond 6 months after termination; internet use for social purposes was associated with decreased perceived social isolation the following year, while instrumental use was not significant. The proposal intends to contextualize ICT effects within living environments and distinguish social vs instrumental vs medical ICT use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and networking expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to disseminate findings via publications and conference presentations and expand professional networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific targets: present at GSA, APHA, SSWR, AAIC, and CTAD; submit conference abstracts; engage with scientific organizations; use conference attendance (~5% effort) to foster collaborations and build reputation for faculty applications.
